findings.title: Task 3 rewrites fleet.ts in full and deletes Part i's HULL_IDS, which schema.ts imports
findings.claim: Task 3 Step 5 says `src/renderer/src/sim/ship/fleet.ts` "becomes:" and then gives the whole file. That file has no `HULL_IDS`. Part i Task 3 Step 4 appends `export const HULL_IDS = ['hound', 'scout', 'valkyrn'] as const;` to fleet.ts, and `schema.ts` gets `import { HULL_IDS } from './fleet'` and `hull: z.enum(HULL_IDS).optional()`. After Task 3 Step 5, schema.ts imports a name that no longer exists, so Task 3 Step 6's `npx tsc -b` fails. The plan never mentions HULL_IDS. Decision 6 also misreads Part i: it says schema.ts may hold quoted ids, but Part i put them in fleet.ts precisely so that it does not.
findings.evidence: plan L669-698 (fleet.ts "becomes:", no HULL_IDS); plan L49 and L704 (Decision 6); Part i plan L50 (Decision 6: HULL_IDS in fleet.ts, Part ii's HullId can be (typeof HULL_IDS)[number]), L870-876 (append HULL_IDS), L878 and L888 (schema imports it, z.enum(HULL_IDS)); current .worktrees/sci-2/src/renderer/src/sim/ship/fleet.ts:1-7
findings.why: Task 3 cannot pass its tsc gate as written. An executor who reads the literal-test output through Decision 6 may also turn `hull` into z.string(), which breaks Part i's valkyrnCrew test (it expects `{ hull: 'cutter' }` to be rejected).
findings.fix: Make Step 5 an append or edit, not a replacement: keep Part i's `HULL_IDS` export and add LINES/FLEET/tubeLoadsItself/SOLO_SHIPS around it. In hullModel.ts, write `export type HullId = (typeof HULL_IDS)[number]` (importing the type from fleet), or keep the literal union and add a test that it equals HULL_IDS. Drop Decision 6's conditional: schema.ts carries no id literal after Part i.

findings.title: pushGunHits infers the shield pop from gunWear instead of Part i's gunHit.stripped
findings.claim: Part i gives the `gunHit` event `stripped: boolean` explicitly for Part ii's shield pop. Part ii's `pushGunHits` ignores it and pops when `s.gunWear === 0` after the frame, and floats `-1` when `s.gunHull === 0`. Events are drained once per frame, and a frame can span several ticks. Two shield hits in one frame where the second is the strip pop twice. A strip followed by another hit pops never. The same applies to hull steps. The test builds events without `stripped`, under `as never`, which hides the type mismatch.
findings.evidence: plan L1960-1972 (pushGunHits), L1774 (test events lack stripped, cast as never); Part i plan L46 (Decision 2: gunHit carries stripped; the view's shield pop reads it), L1660 (event type), L2243-2252 (the sim sets stripped and resets gunWear and gunHull); spec L269-270
findings.why: The shield pop is wrong whenever two hits land in one frame. This is the feedback the spec asks for (§7.4), and the test cannot catch it.
findings.fix: Pop on `e.room < 0 && e.stripped`. For `-1`, either keep the gunHull heuristic and document its limits, or compare the target's hull with its value at the previous frame. Give the test's events a real `stripped` field and drop the `as never`.

findings.title: leadPip's nine-number signature disagrees with Part iii's adapter leadPip(st, 0)
findings.claim: Part ii produces `leadPip(sx, sy, svx, svy, tx, ty, tvx, tvy, speed): Lead | null`. Part iii's tests/valkyrnLead.test.ts calls `leadPip(st, 0)` with a cast, assumes a (state, i) form, and leaves the fix to execution. As written it is a tsc error: 9 arguments expected, 2 given.
findings.evidence: plan L1485 and L1607 (signature); Part iii plan L163, L178-182 (viewOffset calls leadPip(st, 0)), L274 ("If leadPip's signature differs, fix the adapter")
findings.why: The two sibling parts disagree on a produced name's signature, and Part iii's executor has to discover that during execution.
findings.fix: Pin the signature in the shared contract and in Part iii's adapter: `leadPip(s.x, s.y, s.vx, s.vy, t.x, t.y, t.vx, t.vy, GUN_SPEED)`, then subtract the shooter's position. Or have Part ii also export a `leadPipFor(state, i)` wrapper that Part iii calls.

findings.title: The gun's left-button state can stick on when the button is released off the canvas or the window loses focus
findings.claim: `left` is set by the canvas's pointerdown. It is cleared only by the canvas's pointerup, a canvas pointermove with the button bit clear, or `clear()`. The pointer source listens on the canvas only. Press on the map, drag onto the Flight block, Helm block or contact window (DOM over the canvas), and release there: the canvas sees no up or move, so `gunHeld` stays true and the minigun keeps firing until the pointer comes back over the canvas. Alt-tab while holding does the same. Decision 12 acknowledges the canvas gets no moves over the DOM side tools.
findings.evidence: plan L980-986 (leftHeld set and cleared only by canvas handlers and clear), L55 (Decision 12); .worktrees/sci-2/src/renderer/src/app/duel/input.ts:240-244 (listeners on `target`); .worktrees/sci-2/src/renderer/src/app/duel/duelMode.ts:56 (target is the canvas)
findings.why: The pilot overheats and wastes fire they did not ask for. That is a visible control bug on the one new binding the spec centres on (§5.1: left mouse held).
findings.fix: On pointerdown with button 0, call `setPointerCapture` (or add a window-level pointerup/pointercancel listener) and clear `left` on window blur. Add a test: pointerdown on the target, pointerup dispatched on window, then leftHeld() is false.

findings.title: In the Tab ship view the seated pilot's keys still fly the ship (A/D turn and clear the held bearing)
findings.claim: With shipView set, `play` still runs the Flight branch: W/S throttle, F or right-click launch, Q/E. `activeHeld` still sends `moveX` and `face`, so A/D (the walking keys a player reaches for in the interior view) turn the ship and, by Part i's rule, clear holdHeading. Only the gun and the bearing are suppressed.
findings.evidence: plan L1071-1077, L1080-1107 (Flight branch not gated on shipView), L1115-1121 (activeHeld moveX and face unconditional); Part i plan L1369 (A/D or face clears holdHeading)
findings.why: The pilot changes course without seeing the map. The spec leaves input in ship view unstated (§4.4), so the plan should choose explicitly.
findings.fix: Either zero moveX and face and skip the Flight branch (apart from Tab) while shipView is set, or state in Decision 11 that the ship view keeps the Flight bindings, and add a test for the chosen rule.
